name: 蕎美季創 六常庵
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田三崎町2-13-1 田辺ビル 1F
cuisine: An 18-seat hand-cut soba shop that turns into a sake bar at night: two nihachi soba — a fine-cut seiro and a thick whole-grain 田舎 — plus sashimi and fish plates; lunch sets with a kaisen-don or tendon run about ¥1,000–¥1,300, dinner with sake lands around ¥5,000
neighborhood: Kanda-Misakichō 2-chōme, in the Tanabe Building on the Tokyo Dome side of the tracks — 3 min from either the west or east exit of JR Suidōbashi (Chūō-Sōbu line; the Toei Mita and Toei Shinjuku lines also serve the station), 8 min from Jimbōchō on the Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon line. 374 m from Suidōbashi station.
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金 11:30 - 14:15（L.O. 13:40）／17:30 - 22:00（L.O. 21:00）　土・日・祝日 定休日　※東京ドームイベントに応じての営業時間変更有り、詳細はお問い合わせ下さい
gf_detail: Wheat is in the noodle itself. The shop states on its own Facebook page that it cuts two soba — 「細打ちのせいろそばと、殻ごと挽いた玄挽き粉の太打ち田舎そばの二種類、割合はどちらも二八です」 — both at nihachi, i.e. 80% buckwheat to 20% wheat flour, so even the plain seiro is not gluten-free. The same post describes the tsuyu as 「鰹と宗田の粉砕節でひいた出汁と本返しで合わす」, and 本返し is a reduction of soy sauce, mirin and sugar; Japanese soy sauce is wheat by default and no tamari is named. Lunch sets are built around a tendon (wheat batter, shared fryer). There is no gluten-free item here and no wheat-free handling.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu is a katsuobushi and sōda-bushi dashi by the shop's own description, so even a plain cold seiro comes with fish. Tabelog files the kitchen under 魚料理にこだわる — the evening menu is sashimi and fish plates around the sake list. There is no plant-based dashi and no vegan set.

roles: owner-operator (name not published in any source located)
chef_bio.background: The full trading name is 蕎美季創 六常庵 — kyōbikisō rokujōan — and it is a small, deliberately unbranded operation: no website, no phone-book chef profile, an Instagram account (@6jo_an) and a Facebook page that between them carry almost all of the published detail. The room seats 18 across two four-tops and three two-tops, and the soba-cutting bench is in view of the tables, which is the shop's whole argument for itself. Both noodles are cut in-house at nihachi: a fine seiro and a coarse 田舎 milled with the hull on (玄挽き粉), served in two-tier stacks. The dashi is drawn from crushed katsuo and sōda-bushi and married to a honkaeshi. Lunch is the trade — soba paired with a kaisen-don of maguro, shellfish and white fish, or an ebi-and-vegetable tendon, at around ¥1,000, with the hot seiro 大 at ¥1,300 and the cold 田舎もり two-tier at ¥1,200 — and after 17:30 it becomes a soba-ya where you drink, with sake and shōchū the declared specialities and a Tabelog budget band of ¥5,000–¥5,999. It sits three minutes from Suidōbashi station on the Tokyo Dome side, and the shop warns that its hours move with the Dome's event calendar. Nothing about an individual owner-chef is published anywhere located, and rather than guess, this field records that gap.
chef_bio.philosophy: Hand-cut on the premises, in view of the room; two textures of the same nihachi dough rather than one house style.
chef_bio.specialty: 細打ちせいろ and 玄挽きの太打ち田舎そば, both nihachi; kaisen-don and tendon lunch sets; a sake and shōchū list at night.

anecdotes.text: The shop describes its own noodles in one sentence that settles the gluten question: 「細打ちのせいろそばと、殻ごと挽いた玄挽き粉の太打ち田舎そばの二種類、割合はどちらも二八です。鰹と宗田の粉砕節でひいた出汁と本返しで合わす」 — two soba, both eighty-twenty, and a bonito-and-sōda dashi.
Opening hours shift with the Tokyo Dome: Tabelog's own operating-information block carries the shop's warning 「東京ドームイベントに応じての営業時間変更有り 詳細はお問い合わせ下さい」.
Eighteen seats, with the soba-cutting bench visible from the tables — a reviewer counts 4-seaters ×2 and 2-seaters ×3 and notes you can watch the cutting from your chair.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog supplies the exact address (神田三崎町2-13-1 田辺ビル 1F), coordinates, phone (03-5212-6525), genre (そば・居酒屋・日本酒バー), the weekday-only hours with lunch and dinner L.O., the Sat/Sun/holiday closure, the Tokyo Dome hours caveat, 18 seats, all-non-smoking, VISA/Master only, no parking, and the two budget bands. The shop's own Facebook page — read through Yahoo Japan's indexed snippet, the page itself being unreachable to a scripted fetch — gives the nihachi ratio for both noodles and the katsuo/sōda-bushi dashi. A nihon-soba.jp shop write-up (May 2023) gives the 14-seat count as the reviewer saw it and the open soba-cutting bench. A note.com Hongō-lunch column (Oct 2022) gives the set pricing — hot seiro 大 ¥1,300, cold 田舎もり two-tier ¥1,200 — and Retty gives the ¥1,000 kaisen-don set. Yahoo Japan's map card lists the same address and a 3-minute walk from the JR west exit.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Both house noodles are nihachi — 20% wheat flour — so the gluten is inside the soba, not merely alongside it. The lunch sets add a tendon from a shared fryer.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop describes its tsuyu as dashi 「本返しで合わす」. Honkaeshi is soy sauce, mirin and sugar reduced together; ordinary Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and no tamari is named anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The tsuyu is drawn from crushed katsuobushi and sōda-bushi, and Tabelog tags the kitchen 魚料理にこだわる — sashimi and fish plates run all evening.

positives.text: All seats non-smoking, 18 seats only, children and pushchairs admitted, takeout offered, reservations accepted.

cultural_comfort.note: A small local weekday shop three minutes from Suidōbashi station: 18 seats, entirely non-smoking, reservations taken, children and pushchairs welcome, and takeout available. The friction is practical rather than social — no website and no English menu found, cards limited to VISA and Mastercard with electronic money not accepted (bring cash), closed every Saturday, Sunday and public holiday, and hours that move whenever the Tokyo Dome has an event, so phone ahead on event days.

name: 鳥料理 玉ひで
address_ja: 〒103-0013 東京都中央区日本橋人形町1-17-10
cuisine: The 1760 shamo house where oyakodon was invented, reopened November 2025 in a rebuilt 江戸黒 plaster room: Tokyo-shamo gamecock and three eggs bound in a mirin-and-soy tare with no sugar, no onion and no mitsuba — four lunch oyakodon at ¥1,900–¥3,700 (元祖親子丼 ¥2,800), dinner is shamo hotpot courses at ¥6,000–¥8,000
neighborhood: Nihonbashi-Ningyōchō 1-chōme — 1 min from Ningyōchō station exit A2 on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya line, 2 min from Ningyōchō on the Toei Asakusa line and 2 min from Suitengūmae on the Hanzōmon line. 132 m from the station.
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金・土・祝日 11:30 - 13:30／17:00 - 21:30（L.O. 料理 20:30）　日 11:30 - 13:30　※昼の親子丼は13:30までにお並びいただいたお客様までのご案内。日曜日は、月曜日が祝日の場合は夜の営業もあり
gf_detail: The single gluten vector is also the one thing the house will not change. The tare that binds the oyakodon is described in the shop's own press coverage as a blend of high-grade mirin and soy sauce, with the point of pride being 「砂糖や玉ねぎ、三つ葉などは一切使いません」 — no sugar, no onion, no mitsuba. Japanese soy sauce is wheat by default and no tamari or wheat-free soy is named anywhere; the same soy base runs the warishita of the evening shamo-nabe courses. Nothing in the shop's own site, the Yahoo News renewal report or the Tabelog listing mentions allergen handling, a gluten-free option or a substitution policy, and a 266-year-old recipe presented as unchanged is not a recipe that gets altered at the table. Treat it as a no. Note for balance: there is no batter and no fryer in the signature dish, so the barrier is the seasoning alone — but that is enough to make a celiac ill.
vegan_detail: The restaurant is a gamecock house. The signature dish is shamo chicken and three eggs over rice; the evening is shamo sukiyaki and hotpot. There is no plant-based course and nothing in any source suggests one.

chef_bio.origin: Nihonbashi-Ningyōchō, Chūō-ku — the family has traded on this block since 1760
chef_bio.background: Tamahide was founded in 宝暦10年 (1760) as a shamo-nabe house by a family that had served the Tokugawa shogunate as 御鷹匠, falconers — which is where the licence to handle gamecock came from. The dish it is famous for came 131 years later: in 1891 the fifth-generation proprietress, Toku, is credited with pouring the leftover egg-and-broth of a shamo hotpot over rice for a customer in a hurry, and oyakodon was born; NHK has since recognised Tamahide as the originator. The eighth-generation owner, Yamada Kōnosuke, runs it now, and he has spent the last four years rebuilding it: the shop closed in June 2022 for a full reconstruction and stayed shut for three years and three months, reopening on 19 October 2025 and resuming normal lunch and dinner service on 1 November 2025. The new building keeps the trade and changes the room — walls finished in 江戸黒 black plaster, structural beams left exposed, and table seating replacing the old tatami, which makes it materially easier for a visitor with mobility limits than the pre-2022 house was. The cooking did not change. The 元祖親子丼 at ¥2,800 is Tokyo-shamo and three eggs bound in a tare of good mirin and soy sauce and nothing else — the house is explicit that it uses no sugar, no onion and no mitsuba, which is what separates it from the sweeter, onion-bulked oyakodon everyone else serves. Lunch now runs four oyakodon from ¥1,900 (とく親子丼, named for the fifth-generation okami) up to ¥3,700; dinner offers two oyakodon plus the shamo hotpot courses the place was founded on. The lunch queue is the defining experience: the shop stops taking the line at 13:30 and serves whoever is already standing in it.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「砂糖や玉ねぎ、三つ葉などは一切使いません」 — the original oyakodon is shamo, egg, mirin and soy sauce, and nothing is added to make it easier.
chef_bio.specialty: 元祖親子丼 ¥2,800 with 東京しゃも and three eggs; とく親子丼 ¥1,900; a four-strong lunch oyakodon range to ¥3,700; shamo sukiyaki and hotpot courses at dinner; mail-order 鳥すき焼き through kawamata-shamo.com.

anecdotes.text: The oyakodon was not invented by a chef but by the fifth-generation okami, Toku, in 1891 — the leftover egg-and-broth of a shamo hotpot poured over rice for a customer who could not wait. The ¥1,900 entry-level bowl on the new lunch menu is named とく親子丼 after her.
The house closed in June 2022 to rebuild and did not reopen for three years and three months — 19 October 2025 for the soft opening, 1 November 2025 for normal lunch and dinner service.
The family were 御鷹匠, falconers to the Tokugawa shogunate, before they were restaurateurs — the reason a gamecock specialist existed on this block in 1760 at all.

A Yahoo News expert report of 25 October 2025 gives the reconstruction timeline, the 1 November 2025 resumption, the eighth-generation owner's name, the 1891 Toku origin story with NHK's recognition, the new 江戸黒 plaster interior and table seating, the ¥2,800 元祖親子丼 with Tokyo-shamo and three eggs, the no-sugar/no-onion/no-mitsuba rule, and the ¥1,900–¥3,700 lunch range. A 日本橋福徳塾 profile on nihonbashi-tokyo.jp, read via Yahoo Japan's indexed snippet rather than opened directly, identifies the eighth-generation owner and the shogunal falconer lineage.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The oyakodon tare is mirin and soy sauce and nothing else — the house states it adds no sugar, no onion and no mitsuba. Japanese soy sauce contains wheat by default and no tamari is named. The same soy base runs the evening shamo-nabe warishita.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Shamo gamecock and egg are the entire menu, lunch and dinner.

positives.text: The 2025 rebuild replaced tatami with table seating, which removes the floor-sitting barrier the old house had.
Cards (VISA, Mastercard, JCB, AMEX, UnionPay), transport IC, iD, QUICPay and QR payments including Alipay and WeChat Pay are all accepted — unusually easy for a 266-year-old house.

cultural_comfort.note: One minute from Ningyōchō station exit A2, in a building rebuilt in 2025 with table seating rather than tatami, and it takes every card, IC and QR payment a visitor is likely to carry — including Alipay and WeChat Pay. The friction is the queue and the clock: lunch runs 11:30–13:30 and the shop stops accepting the line at 13:30, reservations are taken for dinner only (parties of ten or more by phone), and Sunday is lunch-only unless the following Monday is a public holiday. No English menu is documented, and the room is small and busy at midday. Go at opening or go at dinner.

name: 竹むら
address_ja: 〒101-0041 東京都千代田区神田須田町1-19
cuisine: A 1930 kanmidokoro in a three-storey wooden irimoya house that survived the firebombing — house-made Hokkaidō-bean anko in shiruko and anmitsu, deep-fried agemanjū and awa-zenzai in the cold months, kōri-shiruko shaved ice in summer, almost everything under ¥1,000
neighborhood: Kanda-Sudachō 1-chōme, on the corner in the surviving pre-war block beside Botan and Isegen — 3 min from Awajichō on the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line, 4 min from Ogawamachi on the Toei Shinjuku line and 4 min from Kanda on the Ginza line, 8 min from JR Kanda. 223 m from Awajichō station.
hours_raw: 火・水・木・金・土 11:00 - 20:00（L.O. 19:40）　月・日・祝日 定休日　※営業時間・定休日は変更となる場合があります
gf_detail: The house speciality is the problem: 揚げまんじゅう is a wheat-flour manjū deep-fried to order, so wheat flour and a wheat-loaded fryer are both live in a very small kitchen. The bean sweets are a different matter on composition — the shop makes its own anko from Hokkaidō azuki, and shiruko, awa-zenzai (millet and azuki) and anmitsu (agar, azuki, syrup) contain no wheat by recipe — but no source located publishes an ingredient list, an allergen statement or any cross-contact policy, and there is no evidence the kitchen separates the fryer from the sweet counter. A celiac would need to ask in Japanese, in person, and accept that the answer may be a shrug: this is a three-generation counter that has never been asked. Marked ask, not options, because nothing is documented.
vegan_detail: By composition the core menu reads plant-based — azuki, sugar, agar, millet, kanten, kuromitsu, wheat flour, frying oil — and there is no dashi, no meat and no fish anywhere in a kanmidokoro. But nothing here is verified: the frying oil is not specified, anmitsu variants elsewhere routinely add ice cream or gyūhi, and the shop publishes no ingredient information at all. Treat 'limited' as 'probably fine by recipe, confirmed by nobody' and ask before ordering anything with cream in the name.

chef_bio.background: Takemura opened in 1930 and has not moved, changed hands outside the family, or been rebuilt. The building is the point: a three-storey wooden house in irimoya style with bamboo and plum carved into the second-floor railing and a paper andon lantern reading しるこ hung at the door, one of a tiny cluster in Kanda-Sudachō — with Botan and Isegen next door — that came through the 1945 firebombing intact. Tokyo selected it as a 歴史的建造物 in 2001 and Chiyoda-ku designated it a 景観まちづくり重要物件 in 2003. The third-generation owner, Hotta Masaaki, is in the building from about half past seven every morning, preparing and cleaning, and treats maintaining the structure as part of the job. The kitchen makes its own anko from Hokkaidō azuki to the founding recipe and runs the menu to the season: anmitsu and kōri-shiruko (shaved ice over sweet beans) through the summer, agemanjū and awa-zenzai — the fried manjū and the millet-and-azuki bowl the shop is known for — through the cold half of the year. Almost everything is under ¥1,000. It became conspicuously busier in 2024 when NHK's morning drama 『虎に翼』 used it as the model for the sweet shop its heroine frequents, which is worth knowing before you turn up at a 44-seat cash-only room with no reservations.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep the recipe and the building as they were: the founding-era taste and method, and a wooden house maintained by hand rather than replaced.
chef_bio.specialty: 揚げまんじゅう (deep-fried manjū, made to order); あわぜんざい (millet with azuki); おしるこ with house-made Hokkaidō anko; あんみつ and 氷しるこ in summer.

anecdotes.text: The building survived the Tokyo firebombing along with its immediate neighbours 「ぼたん」 and 「いせ源」 — a pocket of pre-war Kanda that simply did not burn. Tokyo listed it as a selected historic building in 2001; Chiyoda-ku made it a townscape-important property in 2003.
The third-generation owner, Hotta Masaaki, starts at around 7:30 every morning on preparation and cleaning, and counts upkeep of the wooden structure itself as part of running the shop.
NHK's 2024 asadora 『虎に翼』 modelled its kanmidokoro on Takemura, and visitor numbers rose sharply afterwards — expect a queue at a 44-seat room that takes no bookings.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government's 東京歴建 PROJECT feature gives the 1930 founding, the irimoya three-storey wooden construction, the 2001 Tokyo historic-building selection and 2003 Chiyoda townscape designation, the survival of the firebombing, the third-generation owner 堀田正昭 and his morning routine, the bamboo-and-plum railing and しるこ andon, and the 『虎に翼』 connection. Chiyoda-ku's official Visit Chiyoda listing gives the address, phone, Tuesday–Saturday 11:00–20:00 hours with a 19:40 last order, the Sunday/Monday/holiday closure, the station walks, the house-made Hokkaidō-azuki anko and the seasonal split between summer anmitsu and kōri-shiruko and winter agemanjū and awa-zenzai. Tabelog confirms the address 神田須田町1-19, the coordinates, the phone, the 223 m walk from Awajichō, 44 table seats, all-non-smoking, no reservations, cash only, the sub-¥1,000 budget band and its 和菓子・甘味処 百名店 2023 selection.

gf_cross_contamination.text: 揚げまんじゅう is a wheat-flour manjū fried to order, so the shop runs a wheat-loaded fryer in a small kitchen alongside the bean sweets. No separation is documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: No dashi, meat or fish is used anywhere in the menu, but the frying oil is unspecified and no ingredient information is published.

positives.text: All 44 seats are table seating and entirely non-smoking — no floor-sitting, no smoke.
The anko is made in-house from Hokkaidō azuki to the founding recipe, so the bean sweets are a short, transparent ingredient list even without a published allergen sheet.

cultural_comfort.note: Physically easy — 44 table seats, all non-smoking, three minutes from Awajichō, everything under ¥1,000 — but bring cash: no cards, no electronic money, no QR payments, and no reservations. There is no website and no English menu documented, and the room has been noticeably busier since NHK's 『虎に翼』 used the shop as a model in 2024, so expect to wait. Closed Sunday, Monday and public holidays; last order 19:40.
